reviews.text: Plane makes it clear that it isn’t reaching for new heights but it doesn’t wing it either, delivering perfectly acceptable entertainment.
reviews.author: Justin Kim

reviews.text: Part Con Air, part Lost, this is the ultimate Gerard Butler blockbuster - and despite being a disaster movie, it is soothingly unscary.
reviews.author: Francesca Steele

reviews.text: But those who are willing to overlook these missteps in favour of the themes on redemption and perseverance, as well as the confident filmmaking on display, will find themselves greatly rewarded by the film.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: It’s just a solid throwback action thriller that feels like a relic from a bygone era, for all its flaws.
reviews.author: Shakyl Lambert

reviews.text: "Plane" doesn't look like much in its trailers, but the film manages to be a decent popcorn thriller.
reviews.author: Courtney Lanning

reviews.text: Butler + Plane = Awesome
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: Plane is a straightforward movie with very few twists to offer, but the trick to making it engaging lies in its execution. Richet hasn’t made a ton of features, but he’s been in the game long enough to carry out a firm-handed and well-paced effort.
reviews.author: Akos Peterbencze

reviews.text: Nobody’s going to declare Plane a classic, but between Richet’s visual acumen and Butler doing admirable diligence to a character who’s in over his head... it’s an enjoyable, fast-paced and surprisingly engaging diversion.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: Plane is predictable, and its production values are serviceable, but Gerard Butler is comfortably entertaining from beginning to end.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: Plane offers a sometimes breathless, white-knuckle ride that should particularly appeal to those raised on mid-’90s actioners like Con Air, Air Force One and Sudden Death.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: This is pure popcorn entertainment that delivers on nasty-minded action and heroic temperaments that won’t insult your brain cells when you opt to cheer on the unfolding physicality.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: A big part of the fun of Plane - and Plane is a lot of fun - is the way it rapidly cycles through genres fast enough to touch on all the good stuff without ever making it too obvious that we've seen it all before.
reviews.author: Anthony Morris

reviews.text: The plot is hardly innovative -- and some of its more outlandish elements really stretch credibility -- but this is still a gripping enough thriller, boosted by the entertaining lead performances.
reviews.author: Patrick Cremona

reviews.text: Overlook the forced sentimentality and Plane manages to be a taut thriller with a balance of action, blood, shooting, and heroics that seem plausible. You won’t feel silly cheering or cringing and the popcorn will sit satisfied in your belly.
reviews.author: MontiLee Stormer

reviews.text: Solid and enjoyable filmmaking that knows its limits. No overflowing passenger lists, no shoehorned subplots, it does exactly what it says on the tin, and then some. Truly, "redemption can be found in the most unusual places."
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: …Plane is a straight-up, no-nonsense, gritty action flick that delivers plentiful thrills and spills…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Gerard Butler has that Nicolas Cage thing of not phoning in a performance, he's so magnetic in these movies.
reviews.author: JD Duran

reviews.text: If you like well-made action flicks that don’t need a sequel setup, it’s money well spent. Butler knows what he's doing, and Colter excels in a role with a few layers.
reviews.author: Dan Buffa

reviews.text: It's a dumb but entertaining film.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: A film that will be remembered as "that plane movie with Gerard Butler". [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: Plane does not reinvent the wheel but does land an action-movie punch.
reviews.author: Hanna Flint

reviews.text: Plane is a film that is an experience to behold in cinemas, and an entertaining one at that.
reviews.author: Benjamin Wiebe

reviews.text: ... Gerard Butler becomes a worthy heir of the macho hero tradition, the same guy we wouldn't want as a father or a friend, but who comes in handy as a casual 'embedder' or hostage negotiator.
reviews.author: Pablo Vázquez

reviews.text: Conceived to be enjoyed on the big screen, with no more fuss over the proper movement of action and emotion itself. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio F. Pinilla

reviews.text: ... An enjoyable experience for anyone who's an old-school action flick lover seeking simple, to-the-point narratives that don't get overcomplicated. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Plane, much like 1994's "Speed," 2014's "Non-stop," and last year's "Ambulance," is a one-word-titled thriller-adventure-actioner that mostly takes place in a vehicle. Lots of old-school fun.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Plane should have been far more weird and wild than it is, but it’s still a very serviceable and above-average actioner from Jean-François Richet. It doesn’t quite stick the landing, but at least the in-flight entertainment is decent.
reviews.author: Maria Lattila

reviews.text: This one is more solid than you’d expect it to be, refreshingly straightforward and knowing in what its job is and how to execute it without much fuss.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: But Plane is stifled by just how ordinary it is, and how closely it hews to the standard tropes of action films with longer, more descriptive -- yet less ridiculous -- titles.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Even by Butler’s B-list standards, this is borderline inept.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: ... A story that has all the authenticity of a conman's smile, yet unfolds with a kind of crazed energy that might appeal to those looking for hollow popcorn entertainment.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Plane does exactly what it says on the boarding pass. Gerard Butler is the king of big dumb action, getting the tone just right for those in search of uncomplicated thrills.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Entertainingly ridiculous? Or ridiculously entertaining? The slick of wild nonsense slapped over an uninspired undercoat is enjoyable enough while you’re onboard, and then it’s instantly forgettable.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: It may be big, brawling and somewhat inelegant in approach, but this Gerard Butler vehicle is an aviation fuel-powered good time.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: French director Jean-François Richet keeps the action tense, thrilling and reassuringly preposterous.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: It would be easy to nitpick action-thriller Plane for its plot holes, old-school machismo and paint-roller-broad characterisation of Asian villains. But it’s also an adrenaline-pumping banger, skilfully executed by Jean-François Richet
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: Plane plays things resolutely old school, from the electronic score zee-yowing away in the background to the script’s pub quiz sprinklings of pilot jargon, and above all the cartoonish brutality of its violent set-pieces.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: It delivers exactly what you would expect from a Gerard Butler film called Plane – and there’s a simple pleasure to be had in just how thrifty it is at doing that.
reviews.author: Andrew Gaudion

reviews.text: Plane does not reinvent the wheel but does land an action-movie punch.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: It's a thriller with no filler, taking less than two hours to finish, and containing enough tense sequences and shootouts to satisfy any fan of the genre. Add to that a very committed Butler, and we have the winning recipe. Full review in Spanish.
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Richet shines in directing action scenes... Add to that Butler's charisma and the film results in an even film that may not have peak moments worthy of a standing ovation, but neither does it have moments to make you yawn. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillermo Courau

reviews.text: Gerard Butler is a treat – the runtime seems to fly by.
reviews.author: Rafaela Sales Ross

reviews.text: The action is fast-paced, and the hand-to-hand combat is precisely choreographed. Jean-François Richet kept his cool in the editing room and didn't resort to strange cuts to add vertigo to the fights... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: A lack of pretension shouldn’t excuse the utter absence of creative ambition.
reviews.author: Jay Horton

reviews.text: Jean-François Richet keeps the action sleek and the tension high. Butler, meanwhile, has rarely been better.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: This is just the kind of tosh you want it to be. Brisk, easy, brutish. It has explosions, punch-ups, shoot-outs and more than one bit where someone gets smacked in the face with a big hammer. How much more could you reasonably ask? It’s a blast.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: A pleasingly slight and comfortingly formulaic action flick with less plane in it than the title would suggest.
reviews.author: Marc Burrows

reviews.text: A first-rate action thriller.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: What starts in a comfortable disaster-movie mould quickly handbrake-turns into a generic, by-the-numbers action thriller, serving up a stale platter of fist fights, gun battles and hostage-taking.
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: Plane is far from a great action movie but it’s enjoyable enough for what it is.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: Plane is the Ambulance of 2023.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The gloriously named Plane is yet another action movie that showcases the actor’s talents, and proof that they just don’t make ’em like this anymore.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: Plane simultaneously feels as conventional as expected while delivering on some solid intensity and edge-of-your-seat thrills. Butler commands your attention in this surprisingly fun action flick.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: I'm blown away with how fantastic this film is! This is what going to the movies is all about!
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: ...a better-than-expected actioner that feels like a throwback to the similar-themed fare of the 1980s.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: If you don’t take "Plane” too seriously, it’s a hoot, with Butler bringing it in for a smooth landing.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Reminded me of a picture of a beautifully-drawn horse that turned into a stick figure by the end.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: I really enjoyed this in a sort of old school, guilty pleasure kind of way.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: A tight little package delivering enough fun and suspense to elevate this to a standard I hope other Butler action flicks can keep delivering on.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: The film features great action. I mean, Gerard Butler is definitely in his element.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Like an actual commercial aircraft, Plane does not look like much, but it’s also wildly efficient.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: Plane is an unattractive but viscerally effective film. There is little here to admire for the eye, absolutely nothing for the brain, but plenty to appeal to the id.
reviews.author: Melanie Fischer

reviews.text: Truly just one of those movies that is fun and something to suspend your disbelief with for a while.
reviews.author: Rachel Leishman

reviews.text: As it turns out, the film’s title isn’t the most boring thing about it.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: Plane achieves liftoff, and for old-school action fanatics, even if it doesn’t stick the landing, watching it skid wildly off the runway into a ditch with such raucous aplomb is as ridiculous as it is wonderful.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: 'Plane' doesn't soar, but it hovers, entertains, and sticks the landing.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: Plane delivers some decent thrills with two likeable leads. The biggest weakness is the complete lack of character arcs which makes the journey of the main characters feel empty.
reviews.author: Cody Leach

reviews.text: Plane is the perfect kind of movie to rent or stream. The title tells you it's going to be as straightforward as it gets.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: A decent action/survival flick.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Gerard Butler's latest action thriller is simple and silly, yet entertaining and pretty cool throwback to 90's action films. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: As a semi-realistic action movie, Plane delivers exactly what it's supposed to be: pure escapist entertainment full of gripping suspense. The movie has a few twists that don't make the story as predictable as it could have been.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The very definition of a January-ass movie
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: French director Jean-François Richet who gave us the riveting Mesrine gangster films formulates a flight plan filled with thrilling shootouts, fight scenes, and characters I cared about so get out of here Awards Season and extra butter on that popcorn!
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: In this lean action picture, director Richet finds a sleek, take-no-prisoners narrative on which he stages rousing action sequences combined with a small amount of soapy melodrama.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: Plane swoops in to deliver a surprisingly enjoyable ride for a January release. Butler + Colter combo makes for a fun action duo and at just 1 hr and 47 minutes, it’s as efficient as it is thrilling.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: If you're thinking this is just too ridiculous to watch, you're wrong. It's too ridiculous not to watch.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: Plane is a good ol’ action entertainer that’s a breeze to watch and a welcome break if one suffers from superhero or sci-fi fatigue.
reviews.author: Dhaval Roy

reviews.text: If you buy a ticket for this one, just know there’s no First Class option. But with moderate expectations, you’ll still get to your destination.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Going with such a bland title was an odd choice, given that the story is packed with thrills and excitement.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: Gerard Butler’s tough-tender performance is as unassuming and efficient as the film itself.
reviews.author: Nandini Ramnath

reviews.text: Makes some good decisions in style and execution, but its disconcerting tonal shifts make it tedious. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Roberto Landaverde

reviews.text: Surprisingly well made, this Gerard Butler action thriller paints by the numbers but is very good at painting by numbers.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Plane would have been an adequate way to waste a couple of hours lounging on the couch and munching salty snacks. But as a multiplex draw? Not quite, even if you bring the salty snacks along.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Plane says nothing new and reinforces painful cliches, making it feel more like a film from the 1980s or '90s than 2023.
reviews.author: Monique Jones

reviews.text: Plane fall. People fight. Critic happy.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: It's called "Plane" but it could be called "Island" or "Guns" or just "Another Gerald Butler Movie" -- it's entertaining, but it's just that derivative and unexceptional
reviews.author: J. Don Birnam

reviews.text: As rocket launchers are employed, Butler grits his teeth, and the action escalates further, Plane strains credibility. But it does deliver a thrill ride—one that is better for viewers than the passengers.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: For those who simply want to kick back, unplug, and unwind, Butler and company have just what you're looking for.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Plane isn’t a great movie, but it knows what it wants to be. And it’s not letting anything get in its way.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: If you like 1990s action movie throwbacks, you might want to check this one out.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: Just like PLANE no need more word for title, no need more plot for script. PLANE perfect amount story. Gerard Butler perfect in PLANE.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: In a few key moments, the script limitations are lessened by actors like Butler and Goldwyn... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Plane lives and dies on Butler and Colter’s shoulders, and both do a solid job with what they’ve been given.
reviews.author: Nick Johnston

reviews.text: This is basically the January version of [Captain Phillips] — a deceptively relaxing way to simulate and alleviate some New Year’s stress.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: Once the third-act action kicks in, Plane realizes its full potential. Director Jean Francois-Richet... stages the action cleanly and clearly, even though the handheld can be a little too much to handle sometimes.
reviews.author: Matt Lynch

reviews.text: “Plane” is, unquestionably, a profoundly stupid name. It is also all that was available. This script does not operate with adjectives. You cannot find a defining moment or characteristic. I tried to think of a better name, and I truly, genuinely couldn’t.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: Gerard Butler and Mike Colter make a mighty fine action film duo.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: ... generates some white-knuckle tension for the first half-hour before encountering some narrative turbulence.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: This is a species of absurd yet exciting action flicks that have all but vanished into the bargain bin.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: In general, director Jean-François Richet knows how to regulate "Plane‘s" temperature — neither running too hot to further strain the credulity of its stacked consequences nor too cold that it doesn’t get your blood going like an action film should.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: Colter counterbalances all his brawny physicality with a grimly utilitarian sense of humor; moments of Gaspare skulking around corners with a sledgehammer, at least at my screening, drew bigger cheers than Butler’s vein-popping cockpit performance.
reviews.author: Isaac Feldberg

reviews.text: It's a pretty simple story, but all involved milk it for everything it's worth, resulting in a quite intense and gripping, less than two-hour ride be that in the air or on the ground.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Some action fans may find “Plane” a little wanting, but it’s a fun romp that remains engaging throughout its runtime
reviews.author: Simon Thompson

reviews.text: Fans of Butler will find it passable, even if most movie-goers will find it forgettable.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: A more accurate title would... be Island, but Plane is perhaps best at least for instructing audience on the best location to watch the film, half-awake, tipsy on wine served from a litre bottle.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: The highest compliment I can pay the new Gerard Butler action film is that it lives up to the conceptual purity of its title.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: The biggest problem with Plane throughout is that it isn't wilder; it does not revel appropriately enough in its open dumbness.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: While Plane is meant to be a disposable object, the marks of intelligent filmmaking will make it linger as a positive point of comparison against various irritatingly tongue-in-cheek, cartoonish action films of late.
reviews.author: Ethan Vestby

reviews.text: Butler's working man's approach to filmmaking allows him to sell something as basic as Plane, whether he's sharing the screen with Colter or dead sticking an airliner. So if you can, forget the cartoony villains and barely there characters.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: Plane is a knowingly silly action movie with a likable cast and an easy-to-follow narrative. It falls into some old stereotypes but is fun enough for you to ignore the problems and enjoy the ride.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: Destined to become one of TNT’s greatest hits, the Gerard Butler led action vehicle aptly named “Plane,” isn’t as generic as the title may suggest. It’s actually a sturdy, taunt, and crafty little thriller that knows exactly where to steer, er, land.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: In the end, Plane is a high-adventure thrill ride. Unplug your brain. Suspend disbelief and strap in.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: Butler and Colter are natural superstars. If the latter doesn’t have his own cottage industry of actioners on the way, we have failed as a nation.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Sections of the movie recall Die Hard 2 in the best way possible, as Plane delivers thrills and excitement that belie its generic title.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: Fasten your seat belts, turn off your brain and enjoy this bumpy “Plane” ride.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: The very few times Plane leans into being an action film–like the sledgehammer sequence–it is extremely fun, the reason it’s agonizing to watch is the awful dialogue, paper-thin characters, and intelligence-insulting cutaways
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: It seems nobody does it better than Gerard Bulter in the action/thriller genre. The way he sells a story as an actor while dodging bullets always is welcome. With elements of the AIRPORT series, CON AIR and DIE HARD, this is violent but white knuckle fun.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Maybe it's time we give credit to Butler for what he offers, regardless of how singular that may be.
reviews.author: Rachel Ho

reviews.text: It is mostly predictable, and that is just the way we want it... It all works within its own ambitions.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Richet delivers occasional surges of fury in this competent nail-biter, using Butler’s grit in all the right ways.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Nothing more than a Gerard Butler action potboiler, [but] it’s one that’s competently made, delivering the adrenaline rush his fans expect.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Plane is, in essence, the Frontier Airlines of action films: It’s cut-rate to a fault, makes you endure a lot of unpleasantness on the way to its final destination, and still leaves you with the distinct feeling that you didn’t even get what you paid for.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: The overall exercise feels more efficient than inspired, but there's something to be said for that sort of workmanlike ethic in an old-fashioned "B" movie fashion.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: It feels shorter than it is, suggests more than it shows, and gets away with more than it should. Plane is oddly satisfying... could have been a franchise starter back in the eighties... in spite of being completely forgettable.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: Let’s just say this film comes in for a solid landing.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: Sometimes a film without any baggage can -- if not quite soar -- at least make it to the gate on time.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: The best thing that I can say about Plane is that it could have been much, much worse, but it turns out to be an okay action movie.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: The film is funny at times and violent in others, but it lives up to the standard entertainment factor, yielding the first pleasant surprise of 2023.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: This is a wholly competent but only sporadically engaging thriller.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Plane's fight sequences are decent and there are laughs (both intentional and unintentional) peppered through the movie.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Plane feels like being stuck in the middle seat on a long flight.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: A retro guilty pleasure, one that’s as predictable and as lovably dumb as the films it cribs from.
reviews.author: Randy Myers

reviews.text: Like its title, Plane is a tight and to-the-point movie and I had a whole lot of fun watching it.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: This is a pacey item that can be recommended on the grounds that it’s a January release that’s not even close to awful.
reviews.author: Glenn Kenny

reviews.text: We’ve gotten too used to action as mere spectacle, explosions on a video screen. “Plane” takes time — not a lot of time, but just enough — to make this a story about people.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: It ain’t Shakespeare, but if the bread-and-butter movies of Butler’s career were as compactly entertaining and as plausible (granted, a relative term) as Plane, he might get a little more respect.
reviews.author: Steve Davis

reviews.text: Gerard Butler rules the sky in a tense and unrelenting action-thriller. Plane establishes a straightforward premise before plunging into non-stop mortal peril. It's an out-of-the-frying-pan and into-the-fire scenario.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: If you go into it expecting nothing more than to enjoy watching a sweaty Butler manhandle some bad guys while Colter manhandles him, you’ll be more than satisfied with the ride “Plane” offers — a well-executed hunk of pulpy entertainment.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: The stripped-down, unfussy storytelling makes Plane simplistic but entertaining—and refreshingly not contingent on the artificial spectacle that dominates today’s action movies.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: Arguably the best of Hollywood’s old-school action heroes, Butler is in fine macho form in Jean-François Richet’s feature.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: ... Strangely satisfying in its way: flavorful and almost purist in its single-minded focus on delivering empty entertainment calories.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: [Plane is] a dumb title that gets to the point, just like this dumb but very entertaining movie.
reviews.author: Sean Price

reviews.text: It’s noisy, mindless, and violent but endearingly so with thrillingly competent direction, solid character work, and a dose of laughter
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Butler knows what we’re looking for in an action movie, not just the punches and explosions, but the satisfaction of seeing how and by whom the bad guys get dispatched. It shows us that what isn’t new can still be reliably entertaining.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: It’s a return that brings back the unhinged joy of the action movie, but also some of the regressive politics, too.
reviews.author: Alejandra Martinez

reviews.text: This is a substandard Plane movie that never takes off.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: Tedious, shallow and takes itself too seriously while throwing logic, plausibility and fun out of the window. It's just the kind of asinine, paint-by-numbers disaster film that Airplane! has no shame in spoofing.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: There's nothing special about any of this, but as a generic thrill machine, "Plane" certainly delivers the goods.
reviews.author: Soren Andersen

reviews.text: The premise is far-fetched, but director Jean-François Richet's choice to pepper the story with a gritty realism instead of a glossy spectacle makes it work. The simplicity of it all makes the predicament of the characters feel authentic.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: Plane doesn't overcomplicate the plot because the basic threat is exciting enough. The film just takes it seriously to craft a hard-hitting action movie.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: As a somewhat realistic survivalist thriller that steadily pushes its way into the realm of a Rambo episode, Butler's latest picture manages a few striking action sequences and dependable suspense.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Even entering Plane with modest expectations, director Jean-François Richet’s film fails to connect and winds up being as much fun as going through a TSA checkpoint.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Plane is an unpretentious and dependable action film that might not be a first-class experience, but gets audiences from point A to point B with minimal hiccups.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: Actually three films in one, Plane maintains Gerard Butler’s rep as the go-to guy for formulaic, derivative action movies.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: There are about fifteen minutes of fun buried deep in Jean-François Richet’s Plane, but the journey to get there is one that requires wading through a narrative slog that is largely devoid of any prevailing spark.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Manages to be both overstuffed and undercooked, frenzied yet lethargic.
reviews.author: Lena Wilson

reviews.text: It's a movie that delivers exactly what it promises.
reviews.author: Ryan Scott

reviews.text: Its few hints of flair may not cement it as a genre classic, but they’re enough to make it momentarily fun.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: PLANE embraces the things about 90s action movies that made them equally entertaining as they are absurd. If you have money to head to the theater and a deep love of action movies, this is one great way to kick off the year.
reviews.author: Kate Sánchez

reviews.text: Passengers will instead be wishing this flight had been canceled.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: If it were a colour, it would be clear. If it were any less involving than it already is, it would be a blank screen. If it were an object, it would be a rock being used as a paperweight to hold down the scripts of films that might [be worth] making.
reviews.author: Andrew Parker

reviews.text: It’s not that Plane is bad, it’s just so nauseatingly functional that you have to question the circumstances that has led you to watching Plane at all. The only logical conclusion is that you’re on a plane and you’ve got an hour and 47 minutes to kill.
reviews.author: Eric Francisco

reviews.text: This Gerard Butler vehicle is tense and pacy, and consistently delivers fast-moving entertainment through its breezy 100 minute runtime. If audiences want more of these, they will have to show up and support it theatrically.
reviews.author: Ankit Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: In lieu of a real Liam Neeson programmer to soothe the January blues, Plane will do.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: This one’s more pulp than juice, but it’s enjoyable.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: A Dad Movie that could have been produced by The Cannon Group in the ’80s — we aren’t far from The Delta Force. [Full review in French]
reviews.author: Kevin N. Laforest

reviews.text: It is all such gloriously smart stupidity that you cannot help but applaud everyone involved for sticking the landing.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: “Plane” may not take you anywhere you’ve never gone before, but if you’re buying a ticket to a movie called “Plane,” odds are it will get you exactly where you want to go.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: The movie has a likable utilitarian quality, rooted in recognizable behavior, that almost seems to have come out of the pre-Sly-and-Arnold world.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: [Butler] is an engaging, charismatic presence, and Plane is the sort of breathlessly paced suspenser that barely leaves a moment for audiences to stop suspending their disbelief.
reviews.author: Frank Scheck

reviews.text: Plane is a by-the-numbers thriller that, much like the aircraft, has a strong takeoff and a disastrous crash landing.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: A B-level action movie done just right. Expertly crafted to Gerard Butler's strengths.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: A solid dramatic survival thriller with a meaty bromance and explosive climax that includes the repeated devastating deployment of a .50 caliber sniper rifle. What more could you want?
reviews.author: Aaron White

synopsis: In the white-knuckle action movie PLANE, pilot Brodie Torrance (Gerard Butler) saves his passengers from a lightning strike by making a risky landing on a war-torn island -- only to find that surviving the landing was just the beginning. When most of the passengers are taken hostage by dangerous rebels, the only person Torrance can count on for help is Louis Gaspare (Mike Colter), an accused murderer who was being transported by the FBI. In order to rescue the passengers, Torrance will need Gaspare's help, and will learn there's more to Gaspare than meets the eye.
